TEMPORARY — color rendering test

Source: vignettes/articles/test-colors.Rmd
test-colors.Rmd

Checklist — everything listed must show in color (not plain black/white):

  1. Text channel (blue over- / red under-represented cells, several shades):
tab(gss, marital, race, pct = "row", color = "diff")
race
marital White Black Other Total
Married 82% 9% 9% 100% (n=10 117)
Separated 59% 26% 15% 100% (n=   743)
Divorced 79% 15% 6% 100% (n= 3 383)
Widowed 82% 14% 4% 100% (n= 1 807)
Never married 64% 24% 12% 100% (n= 5 416)
NA 76% 12% 12% 100% (n=    17)
Total 76% 15% 9% 100% (n=21 483)
Shades of blue: cells ≥ the Total row +5; +10; +20; +30 points. Shades of yellow to red: cells ≤ the Total row -5; -10; -20; -30 points.
  1. Greyed non-significant cells (.g1/.g2: some cells grey, the rest colored or black):
tab(gss, relig, race, pct = "row", color = "diff", color_signif = "grey_non_signif")
race
relig White Black Other Total
1-Protestant 75% 21% 4% 100% (n=10 846)
2-Catholic 78% 4% 18% 100% (n= 5 124)
3-Other christian 72% 18% 10% 100% (n=   784)
4-Jewish 95% 3% 2% 100% (n=   388)
5-Buddhist/Hinduist 33% 5% 61% 100% (n=   218)
6-Muslim 26% 34% 40% 100% (n=   104)
7-Other 73% 13% 15% 100% (n=   388)
8-None 80% 11% 9% 100% (n= 3 523)
NA 67% 18% 16% 100% (n=   108)
Total 76% 15% 9% 100% (n=21 483)
Shades of blue: cells ≥ the Total row +5; +10; +20; +30 points. Shades of yellow to red: cells ≤ the Total row -5; -10; -20; -30 points. Coloured: significantly different from the Total row (Newcombe score interval, 95% confidence), by at least the first colour threshold. Uncoloured: either not significant, or a difference under ±5 points.
  1. Background channel (.o*/.u*: cell fills, not text):
tab(gss, marital, race, pct = "row", color = c("", "diff"))
race

Widowed 82% 14% 4% 100% (n= 1 807)
Never married 64% 24% 12% 100% (n= 5 416)
NA 76% 12% 12% 100% (n=    17)
Total 76% 15% 9% 100% (n=21 483)
  1. Two channels at once (text + background):
tab(gss, marital, race, pct = "row", color = c("diff", "ratio"))
race
marital White Black Other Total
Married 82% 9% 9% 100% (n=10 117)

NA 76% 12% 12% 100% (n=    17)

Shades of blue: cells ≥ the Total row +5; +10; +20; +30 points. Shades of yellow to red: cells ≤ the Total row -5; -10; -20; -30 points. Background colour (ratio): Cells ≥ the Total row ×1.5; ×2; ×4. Cells ≤ the Total row ÷1.5; ÷2; ÷4.
  1. A regression table (colored ORs, greyed non-significant):
tab_reg(gss, dependent = "married", predictors = c("race", "age", "rincome"))
Logistic regression: married by race, age +1 more
married: 01-Married
levels Model_OR
Reference population 1/4.09***
White 1   
Black 1/2.22***
Other 1.08   
age 1.03***
1-Lt $10000 1   
2-$10000 to 14999 1.15*  
3-$15000 to 24999 1.28***
4-$25000 or more 1.85***
N 12 990
LR vs null <0.01%
McFadden R2 0.049
AIC 17 129

Model: logistic regression; odds ratios (vs the reference category).
Shades of blue: OR ≥ 1.2; 1.5; 2; 4. Shades of yellow to red: OR ≤ 1/1.2; 1/1.5; 1/2; 1/4. Coloured: significantly different from the reference category (Wald interval on the log odds-ratio, 95% confidence), by at least the first colour threshold. Uncoloured: either not significant, or a difference under ×1.2.
***: significantly different from the reference category (in bold) at the 99% confidence level; **: at the 95% level; *: at the 90% level; no star: not significant.
  1. The legend spans under each table were colored even before the fix — they are the control group: if a table above is plain but its legend is colored, the host override is back.
